tier: per-second Linux VM boxes (micro and S/M/L)

free_tier.stated: unverified: no free allowance is stated on the pricing page read; it lists paid per-second box sizes and a USD 20 per month Pro plan
free_tier.notes: The sign-in page offers Google or GitHub sign-in only. The setup instructions say create_box may report that an account needs a card or credit. Whether a new account receives free credit is behind a sign-up.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a Linux VM, not a stored object
per_object_cap.notes: The smallest listed box has a 64 GiB disk; no per-object limit is published.

retention.stated: Idle boxes suspend automatically and resume with state intact; a suspended box is billed only for storage. No automatic deletion timer is stated on the pages read.

egress.terms: Egress rules are a Pro feature: outbound network access can be allowed or denied by destination. No free egress allowance or per-GB price is published on the pricing page read; unverified: egress price

interface_detail: Linux VMs with root access, SSH and preinstalled Docker, Claude Code, Codex and Pi; managed through TypeScript and Python SDKs, an MCP server at https://orble.tech/mcp, and E2B and Daytona compatible endpoints.
tooling: an install script, the orble CLI, the @orble/sdk package for TypeScript and Python, the hosted MCP server, and E2B or Daytona SDKs pointed at Orble endpoints.
chaining: A box can run an agent with a browser and desktop, keep its memory across suspend and fork, and expose a port at a dedicated HTTPS URL; credentials are held outside the VM and injected into outbound requests by the Pro credentials proxy.

limits.value: USD 20 per month Pro plan, or USD 200 per year; boxes billed per second from USD 0.0075 per hour for 1 vCPU, 2 GiB, 64 GiB, suspended boxes USD 0 and storage USD 0.05 per GiB-month
create_box may report that the account needs a card or credit

limits_note: Egress rules, secrets injection, box networks and increased box capacity are Pro features. The egress price and the standard box count ceiling are not published on the pages read.
binding_note: The pricing page publishes no free allowance and the setup instructions warn that box creation may require a card or credit, so that gate decides access before any per-second rate does.

identity_cost.detail: Sign-in offers Google or GitHub sign-in; signing in creates an account. Google and GitHub sign-ins with the same verified email address reach the same account. Whether a card is required to create a box is unverified: the setup instructions say create_box may report that the account needs a card or credit.

reliability_note: Idle boxes suspend automatically and resume with state intact; suspended boxes bill only storage. No SLA or deletion timer is stated on the pages read.

Free credit and the egress price are unverified and would raise the rung if published.

notes: Orble sells per-second Linux VM boxes for AI agents. The published rate is USD 0.0075 an hour for the smallest 1 vCPU, 2 GiB, 64 GiB box; suspended boxes cost nothing and storage is USD 0.05 per GiB-month. No free allowance is published, and the setup instructions warn that box creation may require a card or credit, so the identity gate and prepaid credit bind before the rate. A paid Pro plan at USD 20 a month adds egress rules, secrets injection, box networks and larger fleets. Egress price and any free credit are unverified and would need an account to settle.
